attributes.body:
The expression なん + counter + か in Japanese is a way of highlighting an uncertain number of something, and comes across similarly to 'some', 'several', or 'a few' in English. Literally, the meaning is much closer to 'what + counter + I wonder?', as it shows the speaker's uncertainty about the number.

In addition to なん; いく, from the kanji 幾（いく） (how many/much) may be used as part of this construction. While both are fairly common, 幾（いく） is more common as part of set expressions, like 幾（いく）ら (how much) and 幾（いく）つ (how many/old), while なん is more common for counting specific things, like people.

Both 何（なん） and 幾（いく） are regularly seen in plain hiragana and their kanji forms, so it is worth remembering both.

Caution

Despite having the same kanji as 何（なに）, なん will almost always be used to count things, while なに will be used to identify things.

These patterns are similar in that both combine a counting expression with a particle. Number/Amount + は has a contrastive nuance, implying 'at least' that amount. For example, １０人は来ると思うけど ('I think at least 10 people will come.', implying the speaker is uncertain if any more will.). In contrast, なん + counter + か means 'a few (A)' or 'several (A)', e.g. 何人か 'a few people.'

first_relatable.title: Number/Amount + は
first_relatable.meaning: At least, Sort of, Or so

attributes.body: なん + counter + か is a pattern that combines the question word 何 (なん or なに) with a counter to mean 'a few (A)' or 'some amount of (A)'. For example, 何人か 'a few people.' This is essentially the same as the question word + particle, or 誰か・どこか・誰も・どこも, structure, which is used in expressions such as 何か 'something', 誰か 'someone', and so forth.

attributes.body: These patterns are similar in that both combine a counting expression with a particle. なん + counter + か combines the question word 何 (なん or なに) with a counter to mean 'a few (A)' or 'some amount of (A)', for example 何人か 'a few people.' In contrast, Number + も emphasizes that the number is large, e.g. １０００人も来た ('A whole 1000 people came.')
